key_insight: BrickBench introduces a benchmark for agentic LEGO design that tests whether AI can produce assemblies that are not only semantically aligned with a prompt, but also physically buildable. It evaluates both creative design quality and constraint satisfaction across multiple difficulty settings.
problem_solved: Current text-conditioned design agents can generate plausible concepts, but they often fail at real-world feasibility: choosing compatible parts, respecting local and global assembly constraints, and building something that can actually be constructed from a discrete part library.
method: Defines BrickBench, a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design.
Scores outputs along three axes: validity, alignment, and design quality.
Tests performance across three settings that vary in scale and part availability, forcing joint reasoning over semantic goals and physical constraints.
Provides BrickAgent, an environment for coding and evaluation of design agents.
impact: This matters because it moves evaluation beyond surface-level creativity toward realistic, buildable generative design. For AI/ML practitioners, BrickBench provides a more grounded way to measure agentic planning, constraint reasoning, and embodied design capabilities.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: text prompt → part selection → assembly → scoring

Side-by-side examples of valid vs. invalid LEGO assemblies
Icon set for parts library, constraints, and buildability
paper_authors: Peter Kulits, Yiqing Xu, R. Kenny Jones, Cordelia Schmid, Jiajun Wu
